prompts:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: 16-frame exercise animation sprite sheet for a fitness web app
Primary request: Show ONE adult doing exactly one complete PIKE PUSH-UP repetition. A clean 4 columns × 4 rows grid of 16 equal-size square frames, read left-to-right top-to-bottom. In ALL 16 panels the person is in a high-hip inverted V: both hands planted on the floor, both shoes/toes planted on the floor, knees nearly straight, hips remaining visibly high. Frames 1–4 arms nearly straight at top; frames 5–8 elbows progressively bend and head lowers toward the mat between/slightly ahead of the hands while feet remain fixed; frames 9–12 head reaches low point without touching floor; frames 13–16 elbows extend and person presses back up to the initial inverted V. Clearly show shoulder-loaded vertical pressing, never a horizontal plank or ordinary push-up.
Scene/backdrop: fixed simple light warm-gray studio, a single gray exercise mat, no props.
Subject: same single adult in every frame wearing plain mid-gray T-shirt, charcoal shorts, gray trainers. Anatomically plausible human figure, not a stick figure.
Style/medium: polished naturalistic 3D exercise instruction render, crisp form, subtle soft shadows, consistent camera and lighting.
Composition/framing: fixed side three-quarter camera, whole body including hands, head, both feet fully inside every tile with generous margin; same scale and mat position every frame. A seamless edge-to-edge contact sheet of exactly 4×4 equal panels, no gutters or margins between panels.
Constraints: exact 16 frame tiles in row-major order, one person per tile, obvious movement progression and loop, feet and hands grounded in all tiles, hips high in all tiles, no extra limbs.
Avoid: text, numbers, labels, borders, lines between tiles, arrows, watermarks, blank panels, cropped limbs, normal push-up, plank, hands leaving floor.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: corrected 16-frame fitness exercise sprite sheet
Input image: the supplied 4×4 PIKE PUSH-UP sprite sheet is the edit target.
Primary request: Correct ONLY the last two panels, row 4 column 3 (frame 15) and row 4 column 4 (frame 16). In these two panels the exerciser must finish pressing back to the TOP pike position, both arms straight, head high between upper arms, hips high inverted V, both hands and both feet fixed on the mat. Frame 15 should have straighter elbows than frame 14; frame 16 should match the fully straight-armed first frame. The return in frames 13–16 must progress monotonically upward with no second bend.
Preserve exactly: panels 1–14, 4×4 equal edge-to-edge layout, tile sizes, fixed side camera, same adult in gray shirt/charcoal shorts/gray shoes, same mat/background/lighting, all framing, full body in each tile.
Avoid: changing any other tile, extra people/limbs, blank cells, text, numbering, border lines, gutters, cropping.
assets.assessment: Fixed-camera 4x4 sprite; high hips/inverted V all panels; elbows bend and head lowers, then elbows extend to straight-armed top by frame 16.
assets.caveats: Several near-identical pause frames. Initial version showed a second bend in final two frames; repaired.

prompts:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: 16-frame exercise animation sprite sheet for a fitness web app
Primary request: Show ONE complete bilateral SUPINE SPINAL TWIST stretch cycle in exactly 16 frames. A clean 4 columns × 4 rows grid of equal square panels, read left-to-right top-to-bottom. The same adult lies FACE UP on back on a gray mat throughout, head and shoulders resting on mat, both arms extended wide as a T. Both knees are bent roughly 90 degrees and remain paired together. Frames 1–2 knees upright centered; 3–5 both knees slowly fall to the person's left while both shoulders remain flat; 6–7 hold left twist; 8–9 return knees to center; 10–12 both knees fall to person's right while shoulders remain flat; 13–14 hold right twist; 15–16 knees return upright centered. Both sides must be unmistakable. Camera directly overhead looking down at the mat so left and right knee positions are clear.
Scene/backdrop: fixed simple light warm-gray studio, a single gray exercise mat, no props.
Subject: same single adult in every frame wearing plain mid-gray T-shirt, charcoal shorts, gray trainers. Anatomically plausible human figure, not a stick figure.
Style/medium: polished naturalistic 3D exercise instruction render, crisp form, subtle soft shadows, consistent camera and lighting.
Composition/framing: fixed overhead camera, whole body including hands, head, knees and both feet fully inside every tile with generous margin; same scale and mat position every frame. A seamless edge-to-edge contact sheet of exactly 4×4 equal panels, no gutters or margins between panels.
Constraints: exact 16 frame tiles in row-major order, one person per tile, clearly different left / center / right phases, all shoulders and arms remain on floor, supine face-up throughout, no extra limbs.
Avoid: text, numbers, labels, borders, lines between tiles, arrows, watermarks, blank panels, cropped limbs, prone pose, seated pose.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: corrected 16-frame supine spinal twist exercise sprite sheet
Input image: supplied 4×4 overhead supine spinal twist sheet is the edit target.
Primary request: Rebuild the BENT LEGS / KNEE POSITIONS across the existing 16 panels to make ONE physically coherent bilateral sequence. The adult stays FACE UP, both shoulders remain flat, arms out in a T, both knees bent and touching. Read rows left-to-right:
Row 1 frames 1–4: knees center/upright, then progressively drop to the VIEWER'S LEFT.
Row 2 frames 5–8: knees remain on VIEWER'S LEFT for frames 5–6, then rise through center and reach CENTER at frame 8.
Row 3 frames 9–12: knees begin CENTER then progressively drop to the VIEWER'S RIGHT.
Row 4 frames 13–16: knees remain on VIEWER'S RIGHT for frames 13–14, then rise to CENTER for frames 15–16.
The legs should never alternate left/right unexpectedly. One side, center, other side, center. In every tile keep knee pair and both feet anatomically attached and visible.
Preserve: exact seamless 4×4 equal-size contact sheet, identical gray-clothed adult, head/torso/shoulders and wide T arms, gray mat, overhead camera, background/lighting, full-body framing.
Avoid: text, numbers, borders, gutters, arrows, blank panels, extra limbs, cropped hands/feet, shoulders lifting, prone pose.

Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: looping 16-frame fitness animation contact sheet
Primary request: An anatomical overhead photo-real exercise guide for SUPINE SPINAL TWIST. Exactly 4 columns and 4 rows of equal square animation frames. Read left-to-right, row by row. One adult lies face-up with shoulders flat on a gray mat, arms spread in a horizontal T, knees bent 90 degrees and held together. Camera fixed directly overhead. The torso, shoulders and arms remain identical in every tile. Only the joined bent knees/feet rotate across the abdomen.
IMPORTANT FOUR-ROW ACTION MAP:
ROW 1, four frames: knees point UP at center → a little to IMAGE LEFT → farther IMAGE LEFT → fully resting to IMAGE LEFT.
ROW 2, four frames: knees stay fully to IMAGE LEFT → a little less left → near center → point UP at center.
ROW 3, four frames: knees point UP at center → a little to IMAGE RIGHT → farther IMAGE RIGHT → fully resting to IMAGE RIGHT.
ROW 4, four frames: knees stay fully to IMAGE RIGHT → a little less right → near center → point UP at center.
Thus all of rows 1–2 are LEFT or CENTER only, all of rows 3–4 are RIGHT or CENTER only. No knee positions on image right in rows 1–2; no knee positions on image left in rows 3–4.
Scene/backdrop: neutral warm-gray studio, single gray mat, no props.
Subject: same single adult in all tiles wearing mid-gray T-shirt, charcoal shorts, gray trainers.
Style: polished naturalistic 3D exercise instructional render, anatomically realistic adult, no stick figures.
Composition: overhead view with whole body, both outstretched hands, both feet entirely in each tile with margin, same scale and position in all tiles, 16 seamless equal tiles without gutter.
Avoid: text, numbers, labels, borders, tile divider lines, arrows, watermarks, blank panels, extra limbs, kneeling, prone positions, alternating left/right knee direction within a row.
assets.assessment: Fixed overhead 4x4; rows 1-2 center to image-left and back; rows 3-4 center to image-right and back; paired bent knees, shoulders down and T arms.
assets.caveats: Hands approach tile edges; first two versions had incorrect side order.

Same adult kneels on a mat with knees bent and hips resting back near heels, chest low toward the mat and arms reaching far forward throughout. BOTH sides need to be obvious with sideways arm positions and long asymmetric torso lines, not a generic forward reach.

Subject: same single adult in every frame wearing plain mid-gray T-shirt, charcoal shorts, gray trainers. Anatomically plausible human figure, not a stick figure.

Composition/framing: fixed elevated rear three-quarter camera looking slightly down toward the outstretched hands so the left/right hand-walk is visible, whole body including hands, head, knees, hips and both feet fully inside every tile; same scale and mat position every frame. Seamless edge-to-edge contact sheet of exactly 4×4 equal panels, no gutters or margins between panels.
Constraints: exact 16 frame tiles in row-major order, one person per tile, visibly low child's pose with hips on heels throughout, no extra limbs.

prompts:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: 16-frame exercise animation sprite sheet for a fitness web app
Primary request: Show ONE complete PRONE HALF FLOOR ANGEL repetition in exactly 16 frames. A clean 4 columns × 4 rows grid of equal square panels, read left-to-right top-to-bottom. Same adult lies FACE DOWN on the abdomen and chest on the exercise mat throughout; pelvis and legs remain planted and still. With both arms hovering just a few centimeters ABOVE the floor, symmetrically sweep the arms in wide shallow semicircles from alongside the hips/thighs outward to shoulder height and then to a bent-elbow W position near the head/ears (a half snow-angel range, small controlled shoulder motion). Then reverse the same sweeping path back down alongside the hips. Frames 1–2 hands beside hips, frames 3–6 arms arc gradually outward/upward, frames 7–8 reach bent-elbow W/high half-angel, frames 9–14 sweep gradually back, frames 15–16 hands beside hips. Arms visibly change angle frame by frame while torso remains low; elbows do not row toward ribs.
Scene/backdrop: fixed simple light warm-gray studio, a single gray exercise mat, no props.
Subject: same single adult in every frame wearing plain mid-gray T-shirt, charcoal shorts, gray trainers. Anatomically plausible human figure, not a stick figure.
Style/medium: polished naturalistic 3D exercise instruction render, crisp form, subtle soft shadows, consistent camera and lighting.
Composition/framing: fixed directly overhead camera looking down on the person's back, whole body including both hands, head and both feet fully inside every tile with generous margin; same scale and mat position every frame. Seamless edge-to-edge contact sheet of exactly 4×4 equal panels, no gutters or margins between panels.
Constraints: exact 16 frame tiles in row-major order, one person per tile; prone torso fully grounded throughout, arms only hover a little and sweep to W then back, no extra limbs.
Avoid: text, numbers, labels, borders, lines between tiles, arrows, watermarks, blank panels, cropped limbs, Superman back extension, chest lifting, rowing motion, arms straight into full overhead Y.
assets.assessment: 4x4 fixed overhead; chest/abdomen grounded; arms make a small controlled sweep from beside hips to T/bent W and back.
assets.caveats: Actual depicted movement is hips-to-W-to-hips, not overhead-Y-to-W. Integration cue must match that specific half-range path. Panels equal but rectangular due output dimensions.
